trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the Aerobus (€6.75 one-way) or L9 Sud metro line (€5.15) to the city centre, then connect via L3 (green line) toward Sant Just Desvern. Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona. After settling in, take a short stroll around the Sant Just Desvern neighbourhood to get your bearings and grab a casual dinner nearby.

meals.lunch: N/A – on the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Bar-restaurant near the hotel in Sant Just Desvern – look for a local 'menú del día' (evening version) or a neighbourhood tapas bar. Budget ~€10–14 for a set meal with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – you'll be tired from travel. Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) at the airport or any metro station; it covers all metro, bus and tram rides within Zone 1 and is the most budget-friendly way to get around. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance as arrival is after 19:00.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Take the metro (L3 green line) from Zona Universitària to Diagonal, then L5 to Sagrada Família (approx. 30 min from hotel area). Arrive early (~9:00) to beat the heat (high of 28.9°C). The skip-the-line guided tour lets you explore Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica in depth, including the towers and museum. Book tickets online in advance (~€26–32 with tower access) to save time and money.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, walk 15 minutes north to Park Güell & Gràcia Neighbourhood Exploration. Visit Gaudí's whimsical mosaic-covered park with its iconic dragon staircase and panoramic terraces overlooking the city. The Monumental Zone requires a ticket (~€10, book online); the surrounding park is free. Afterwards, wander down into the charming Gràcia neighbourhood – browse its bohemian squares like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Eixample district (a short metro ride) to explore the famous 'Gayxample' area and its vibrant bar scene. Start with vermouth ('vermut') at a classic Eixample bar around 19:00, then enjoy the lively street atmosphere. For nightlife, check out Carrer del Consell de Cent or Carrer de Muntaner for affordable cocktail bars and clubs that warm up after 23:00.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant or 'pa amb tomàquet' (bread with tomato) at a local café near the hotel or near Sagrada Família – budget ~€3–5.
meals.lunch: Menú del día near Gràcia neighbourhood – a 3-course lunch with bread and drink for ~€12–14. Look for chalkboard signs outside restaurants.
meals.dinner: Affordable pintxos or tapas bar in Eixample – order from the bar to keep costs down. Budget ~€10–15 including a beer or glass of house wine.

day_by_day.notes: August is peak season – book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online at least a few days ahead to avoid sell-outs and long queues. Wear sunscreen and carry a water bottle; 28.9°C in the afternoon can feel intense. The Monumental Zone of Park Güell has timed entry slots.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour – Take the metro to Jaume I (L4 yellow line). Join a free walking tour of Barcelona's medieval heart (tip-based, budget €5–10 tip). Discover Roman ruins, the Barcelona Cathedral, hidden plazas like Plaça de Sant Felip Neri, and the old Jewish quarter (El Call). Tours typically start around 10:00 and last 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Gothic Quarter, walk 10 minutes to El Born neighbourhood. Visit the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar (free entry) – a stunning Gothic church and architectural gem. Explore the Born Cultural Centre (free or low-cost) which houses excavated ruins of the 1714 siege. Stroll along the Passeig del Born and browse the independent boutiques and street art.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Barceloneta beach (15-min walk from El Born) for a sunset stroll along the seafront promenade. As night falls, explore the beach bars ('chiringuitos') for a cold beer (~€3–4). Later, move to the El Born or Barceloneta nightlife strip – bars and clubs here are lively from 22:00 onwards. Try Razzmatazz (one of Barcelona's most famous clubs, entry ~€12–15) or smaller bars on Carrer del Parlament in Sant Antoni.

meals.breakfast: Café con leche and a 'napolitana' pastry at a local bakery near the Gothic Quarter metro stop – ~€3–4.
meals.lunch: Mercat de Santa Caterina (near El Born) – grab fresh produce, local cheeses, olives and a bocadillo from market stalls for a self-assembled picnic lunch. Budget ~€6–9.
meals.dinner: El Born neighbourhood – look for a set dinner menu or a budget-friendly Catalan restaurant. Try 'pa amb tomàquet', croquetes and patatas bravas. Budget ~€12–16.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter can be very crowded mid-morning in August – the walking tour helps you navigate efficiently. Keep an eye on your belongings in tourist-heavy areas. Barceloneta beach gets busy; arrive at sunset for a more relaxed atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc Hill Architecture & Art Morning – Take the metro to Paral·lel (L2/L3) then the free Montjuïc funicular (included with metro card). Explore the Fundació Joan Miró exterior and gardens (entry ~€14, or admire the architecture from outside to save money). Walk to the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe – the iconic 1929 Barcelona Pavilion, a masterpiece of modernist architecture (entry ~€7). Also visit the Jardins de Laribal (free) for shaded terraces and fountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the cable car down to the Poble Sec neighbourhood. Explore Carrer de Blai – Barcelona's famous 'pintxos street' – for an early afternoon snack. Then head to the Eixample district to do the 'Manzana de la Discordia' (Block of Discord) self-guided walk along Passeig de Gràcia, admiring the exteriors of Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller and Casa Lleó Morera (exterior viewing is free; interior entry is expensive but optional). Walk up to Casa Milà (La Pedrera) and admire its undulating stone façade.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Eixample or Sant Antoni neighbourhood for Barcelona's thriving cocktail bar and craft beer scene. The Mercat de Sant Antoni area (recently renovated) has excellent budget bars and a young local crowd. Enjoy a 'vermut' hour from 19:00–21:00, then transition to a bar crawl along Carrer del Parlament. Clubs in this area open around midnight.

meals.breakfast: Café and toast with olive oil and tomato at a bar near Paral·lel metro – ~€3–5.
meals.lunch: Carrer de Blai pintxos – grab 4–6 pintxos and a beer for ~€8–12. Arrive between 13:00–14:00 for the freshest selection.
meals.dinner: Poble Sec or Sant Antoni – find a neighbourhood restaurant with a menú del día (evening version) or a casual Catalan eatery. Budget ~€12–15.

day_by_day.notes: Montjuïc is best visited in the morning before the heat peaks. The funicular is included in your T-Casual metro card – no extra cost. If budget allows, the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe is a must for architecture lovers and is very affordable. Passeig de Gràcia exteriors are completely free to admire.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana – Take the metro to Urquinaona (L1/L4). Visit this UNESCO World Heritage modernista concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner – one of Barcelona's most breathtaking architectural interiors. Guided tours run from 09:00 (~€22) or opt for a self-guided visit (~€18). Book online in advance. Afterwards, explore the surrounding El Born streets and the Arc de Triomf (free, 10-min walk).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a relaxed final afternoon at Barceloneta Beach or Poblenou Beach (quieter alternative, 15-min walk north). Swim, relax and soak up the Mediterranean sun. Alternatively, visit the free Parc de la Ciutadella – stroll through the park, see the monumental cascade fountain (partly designed by a young Gaudí), and rent a rowboat on the lake (~€6 for 45 min). A perfect, low-cost way to spend a hot August afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Barcelona – head back to El Born or the Gothic Quarter for a farewell dinner. Splurge slightly on a sit-down Catalan meal (budget ~€18–22 with wine). Afterwards, enjoy one last night out: rooftop bars in Eixample offer stunning city views (many have free entry with a drink purchase ~€8–10). End the night at a live music venue or club of your choice – Barcelona's nightlife runs until 05:00–06:00 on weekends.

meals.breakfast: Full café breakfast near the hotel before heading into the city – coffee, orange juice and toast with tomato ~€5–7.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Parc de la Ciutadella or a beach chiringuito – grab supplies from a nearby Mercadona supermarket (sandwich, fruit, drink) for ~€5–7.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in El Born or Gothic Quarter – a sit-down Catalan restaurant with 'pa amb tomàquet', fresh seafood or 'fideuà' (noodle paella). Budget ~€18–22 per person including house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Palau de la Música tickets sell out quickly in August – book online as soon as possible. If you have an early departure the next day, plan your nightlife accordingly and pre-arrange your airport transfer. The Aerobus runs from Plaça de Catalunya and is the easiest budget option back to the airport (~€6.75). Keep €20–30 aside for last-minute souvenirs or unexpected costs.

day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit. Flight lands at El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the Aerobus or taxi (~25 min) to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Casual stroll around Sant Just Desvern town center to stretch your legs after the flight. Explore the quiet local streets, grab a drink at a nearby terrace bar, and wind down. Early night recommended to prepare for full days ahead.

meals.lunch: N/A – on the plane or airport
meals.dinner: La Bodega de Sant Just (local neighbourhood restaurant near the hotel) – try a simple menú del día or tapas plate with local wine. Budget ~€15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Sant Just Desvern is a quiet residential suburb ~10 km from central Barcelona. The hotel is well connected by bus (L57, L58) and taxi. Keep luggage light for the evening walk. August evenings are warm (~22–24°C) so a light layer is enough.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Take the L57 bus or a taxi into central Barcelona (approx. 20–25 min). Arrive early (9:00–9:30 AM) for your skip-the-line guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Spend 1.5–2 hours marvelling at the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like interior columns, and the towers with panoramic city views. Book tickets in advance online (~€35–45 with tower access).
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration – Head uphill to Park Güell (15 min by taxi or Bus 116 from Sagrada Família). Explore the mosaic dragon staircase, the Hypostyle Room, and the panoramic terrace overlooking the city. Afterward, descend into the charming Gràcia neighborhood for a leisurely wander through Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia. Browse independent boutiques and enjoy the bohemian atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Tapas Crawl & Vermouth Hour in El Born – Head to the El Born district (metro L4 to Jaume I). Begin with a classic vermouth (vermut) at Bar Marsella or El Xampanyet, then hop between tapas bars sampling patatas bravas, croquetas, pan con tomate, and fresh anchovies. Finish with a nightcap at a rooftop bar in El Born.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café in Sant Just Desvern – croissant, café amb llet, and fresh orange juice (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana near Passeig de Gràcia – excellent tapas and montaditos in a lively setting (~€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Self-guided tapas crawl in El Born – budget ~€25–35 per person across 3–4 stops including drinks

day_by_day.notes: August is peak season – book Sagrada Família tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance. Park Güell's monumental zone also requires timed tickets (~€10). Wear comfortable walking shoes. Stay hydrated – daytime highs around 29°C. Carry a small water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour – Take the metro (L3 from Zona Universitària or bus into centre) to the Gothic Quarter. Join a guided walking tour (many depart from Plaça de Catalunya at 10:00 AM, ~€15–20 for a small group tour). Discover Roman walls, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, the old Jewish Quarter (El Call), and hidden medieval plazas. The tour typically lasts 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta Beach & Waterfront – After the tour, walk 15 minutes south to Barceloneta Beach. Spend the early afternoon relaxing on the sand, swimming in the Mediterranean, or renting a paddleboard (~€15/hr). Walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade, visit the Frank Gehry fish sculpture, and explore the Port Olímpic marina area. Take a break at one of the beach chiringuitos (beach bars) for a cold drink.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach Sunset & Nightlife on Passeig Marítim – Return to Barceloneta for golden hour (sunset around 8:45 PM in August). Watch the sun dip over the city skyline from the beach. As night falls, transition into the Passeig Marítim nightlife scene – visit a beach club or open-air bar. For a more vibrant night, head to Opium or Pacha Barcelona (entry ~€15–20, often includes a drink).

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in El Raval (near Gothic Quarter) – avocado toast, specialty coffee (~€10–14)
meals.lunch: La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta (cash only, arrive early – famous for the original bombas tapas, ~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: La Mar Salada near Barceloneta – fresh seafood paella and grilled fish with sea views (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Barceloneta gets very crowded in August – arrive at the beach before noon for a good spot. Keep valuables secure in the Gothic Quarter (pickpocket hotspot). Beach clubs may have dress codes in the evening – smart casual recommended. Check sunset time and plan to be on the beach 30 min before.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana & El Born Architecture – Start the morning with a guided tour of the stunning Palau de la Música Catalana (UNESCO World Heritage Site), a masterpiece of Catalan Modernisme by Lluís Domènech i Montaner (~€22, tours at 10:00 AM). Marvel at the stained-glass ceiling and ornate concert hall. Afterward, walk through El Born's streets to admire the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar, a stunning Gothic church with a serene interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Eixample District & Modernisme Architecture Walk – Head to the Eixample district (metro L2/L3 to Passeig de Gràcia). Walk the 'Block of Discord' (Manzana de la Discordia) to see three rival Modernisme masterpieces side by side: Casa Batlló (exterior or interior tour ~€35), Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera. Continue to Casa Milà (La Pedrera) for a rooftop tour with iconic chimneys and city views (~€28). Browse the elegant Passeig de Gràcia boulevard.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop Bar Hopping in Eixample – Eixample has some of Barcelona's best rooftop bars. Start at the La Pedrera rooftop evening event (check for summer night sessions ~€38 with cava) or head to Hotel Majestic's rooftop bar. Then explore the 'Gayxample' area around Carrer del Consell de Cent for vibrant bars and a lively nightlife scene. End the night at a cocktail bar on Carrer de Muntaner.

meals.breakfast: Bar Calders in Sant Antoni market area – traditional Catalan breakfast with pa amb tomàquet and coffee (~€7–10)
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana or Parking Pizza in Eixample – mid-range, lively atmosphere (~€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda in Eixample – cosy wine bar with excellent charcuterie boards and natural wines (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Casa Batlló and La Pedrera tickets online in advance to avoid queues. The Eixample grid is very walkable but distances add up – consider a Bicing bike share (day pass ~€5) to move between sites. Evening rooftop bars fill up fast in August – arrive by 8:00 PM or book ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc Hill & Pavilion Mies van der Rohe – Take the Montjuïc cable car or Bus 150 up to Montjuïc. Visit the Barcelona Pavilion (Mies van der Rohe's 1929 masterpiece of modern architecture, ~€12) and the Fundació Joan Miró for a dose of contemporary art (~€15). Enjoy panoramic views of the city and port from the Castell de Montjuïc (free to walk the grounds).
day_by_day.afternoon: Mercat de Sant Josep de la Boqueria & El Raval – Descend from Montjuïc and head to La Boqueria market on La Rambla for a sensory overload of fresh produce, jamón, seafood, and local cheeses (best for browsing and snacking, not a sit-down meal). Explore the El Raval neighbourhood – visit the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art, ~€12) or simply enjoy the street art and multicultural atmosphere. Stop at a terrace café for a mid-afternoon break.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Final Night Out – For your last evening, treat yourself to a memorable dinner in El Born or Eixample. After dinner, head to one of Barcelona's iconic nightlife venues – Sala Apolo for live music or a club night, or Bar Marsella (one of Barcelona's oldest bars, dating to 1820) for a historic nightcap. End the trip on the terrace of a rooftop bar watching the city lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Forn de Sant Jaume bakery near the hotel – fresh pastries and coffee (~€6–9)
meals.lunch: Quimet & Quimet in El Raval – legendary standing tapas bar, famous for creative montaditos and canned seafood (~€15–20 per person, cash only)
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born – classic Catalan restaurant with house cava and traditional dishes (~€30–40 per person) or splurge slightly at Bodega 1900 by Albert Adrià (~€45–55)

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is extremely crowded mid-morning – visit before 11:00 AM or after 2:00 PM. If rain occurs (possible ~47mm across the month), Montjuïc and indoor museums are great wet-weather alternatives. Pack a light rain jacket just in case. For the return journey, check bus/taxi times from the hotel to El Prat Airport – allow 45–60 min during peak hours.

meals.dinner: Barraca Restaurant on Barceloneta beachfront – upscale Mediterranean seafood with stunning sea views. Try the paella negra or fresh grilled catch of the day. Book a terrace table for sunset dining.

Discover Roman ruins beneath the city, the stunning Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden plazas that most tourists miss. day_by_day.afternoon: Tapas Crawl & Vermouth Hour in El Born – After the Gothic Quarter, transition seamlessly into the adjacent El Born neighbourhood for a self-guided premium tapas crawl. Visit Bar del Pla for modern Catalan tapas, El Xampanyet for house cava and anchovies, and end with vermouth at Bar Marsella (one of Barcelona's oldest bars, est. 1820). Explore the stunning Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar and the Picasso Museum (book tickets in advance) in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop Bar Hopping in Eixample – Experience Barcelona's sophisticated rooftop bar scene. Start at the Mandarin Oriental's Terrat rooftop bar for panoramic Eixample views and expertly crafted cocktails, then move to the Hotel Arts Sky Bar for elevated Mediterranean vibes. End the night at Dry Martini Barcelona, an iconic cocktail institution beloved by locals and connoisseurs alike.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Parking Pizza (Carrer de de Londres) or Flax & Kale for a premium health-forward breakfast with fresh juices and eggs Benedict.
meals.lunch: El Xampanyet (El Born) – legendary local bar serving house cava, anchovies, and traditional tapas in an authentic setting. Arrive at 13:00 sharp as it fills quickly.
meals.dinner: Disfrutar Restaurant – one of Barcelona's most celebrated fine-dining establishments (ranked among World's 50 Best Restaurants). Avant-garde tasting menu by former elBulli chefs. Book months in advance. Alternatively, Lasarte (3 Michelin stars) for refined Basque-Catalan haute cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot – wear comfortable shoes as cobblestones can be uneven. Private guided tours can be arranged through the hotel concierge or platforms like Viator/GetYourGuide. Fine dining reservations at Disfrutar or Lasarte must be booked well in advance – confirm before departure from home.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc & Palau Nacional (MNAC) – Take the Montjuïc cable car or funicular up to the hill overlooking the city. Visit the Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya (MNAC) housed in the magnificent Palau Nacional, home to the world's finest collection of Romanesque art. Explore the surrounding gardens and enjoy sweeping views over Barcelona's skyline and port. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró for world-class modern art in a stunning rationalist building.
day_by_day.afternoon: Architectural Deep Dive: Modernisme Route – Hire a private driver or join a premium architecture tour to explore Barcelona's Modernisme gems beyond Gaudí. Visit Casa Batlló (book the premium 'Magic Nights' evening experience or daytime tour with AR features), Casa Lleó Morera, and Palau del Baró de Quadras. Walk the Passeig de Gràcia 'Block of Discord' and admire the facades of competing architectural masterpieces.
day_by_day.evening: Casa Batlló Magic Nights or Palau de la Música Catalana Concert – If not visited in the afternoon, attend the Casa Batlló Magic Nights immersive evening experience (runs in summer, check schedule). Alternatively, attend a classical or flamenco concert at the UNESCO-listed Palau de la Música Catalana – one of the world's most breathtaking concert halls, designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Dress smartly.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit Forn de Sant Jaume (Passeig de Gràcia) for premium Catalan pastries, croissants, and coffee in an elegant setting.
meals.lunch: Tickets Bar (Albert Adrià's tapas bar, El Poble Sec) – playful avant-garde tapas in a circus-themed setting. Book well in advance. Alternatively, Bodega Sepúlveda for traditional Catalan wine-bar lunch.
meals.dinner: Moments Restaurant at Mandarin Oriental Barcelona – 2 Michelin-star Catalan haute cuisine by chef Raül Balam. Elegant setting, impeccable service, and a wine list featuring the finest Catalan and Spanish labels. Perfect for a special evening.

day_by_day.notes: Casa Batlló Magic Nights tickets sell out fast in August – book online immediately. The Palau de la Música Catalana concert schedule is published monthly; check their official website. Montjuïc is best visited in the morning before peak heat. Bring a light layer for air-conditioned museums.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure Morning & Spa – After four packed days, enjoy a slow luxury morning. Indulge in a spa treatment at the hotel or book a session at a premium day spa such as Aire Ancient Baths (El Born) – a stunning Roman-inspired thermal bath experience with aromatherapy pools, steam rooms, and optional massage treatments. Book the 'Ritual' package for the full experience. Perfect for sore feet and travel fatigue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Poblenou & 22@ Innovation District Architecture Walk – Explore Barcelona's cutting-edge contemporary architecture in the Poblenou district, the city's reinvented industrial neighbourhood. Walk along Rambla del Poblenou, visit the iconic Torre Glòries (Jean Nouvel's luminous tower), and explore the @22 tech district's striking modern buildings. End at the Rambla del Poblenou for a final afternoon coffee and people-watching. Visit the Palo Alto Market if it falls on a weekend.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Final Night Out – Celebrate the final evening with a memorable farewell dinner followed by Barcelona's legendary late-night scene. After dinner, head to one of Barcelona's most exclusive clubs: Pacha Barcelona, Opium, or the rooftop of W Barcelona (Eclipse Bar) for cocktails with panoramic sea views. Dance until dawn – this is Barcelona, after all.

meals.breakfast: Slow hotel breakfast or visit Federal Café or Syra Coffee for specialty third-wave coffee and premium pastries.
meals.lunch: Rías de Galicia (Carrer de Lleida) – one of Barcelona's finest seafood restaurants, celebrated for Galician-style shellfish, percebes (barnacles), and fresh Atlantic fish. A true luxury seafood experience.
meals.dinner: Enoteca Paco Pérez at Hotel Arts Barcelona – 2 Michelin-star Mediterranean fine dining with stunning port views. Exceptional tasting menu pairing Catalan ingredients with creative technique. Request a window table overlooking the marina for a magical farewell to Barcelona.

day_by_day.notes: Aire Ancient Baths must be booked in advance – slots fill quickly in August. If departing the next morning, pack bags the night before and confirm checkout time with the hotel. W Barcelona's Eclipse Bar is one of the city's most iconic spots for a final nightcap with 360° views. Keep the evening flexible – Barcelona's magic often happens spontaneously.
